Hi Guys,

here is my homework on FL. More screenshots will follow in next posts.

I have concentrated on FL which built on the broken S/R level as I saw them working best and being the most obvius ones. There are a lot FL building far away from the S/R level, especially in strong trending conditions. They tend to not work as good as the ones situated at the broken S/R.

What I have ebserved so far: - Going with the trend will produce the best FLs and increase the odds of working - The immediate FTB is usually the best chance to suceed - Price will very often bounce from the S/R level which got broken creating the FL - Tighter FL seem to work better than wider once - Once the FL gets engulfed/broken, price tends to go to the next swing low/high (FTR). Sometimes it goes there directly but most of the time it retraces first

Hi John,

this question is bothering many of us, including me. The problem is, we are looking for perfection, for something what works 100% of the time. I think, one is only wasting the time doing it. How many weeks, months, years are we wasting looking for answers in forums with clear rules wich work 100% of the time? This is a process oriented approach and you have some very good rules here which you have to build on. But to do, you have to do your own research. There is no way around it. No short cuts. If you take one rule from marketpedia and and go over charts and use the rule in a consistent manner (you use this rule the same way every time), you will get results in terms of if it works or not, in which circumstances etc. You then come to the conclusion, how to trade it. If it for example doesn't work 80% of the time, that's perfect, because you know that when you do the opposite, it will work What I am trying to say is, stop wasting the time searching for perfection and start working on your own unique style, which will work for you and which you will understand because you have built it from the scratch. The process counts.

The other thing which is stopping us from improving is the endless searching for 100% accuracy, when there simply is no need for 100% accuracy. We have to accept that we won't be right every time and that is fine because we can still make money.

Take something what you think you understand or what you like and do as detailed research on it as you can, then build on it. That's really it:)
